outcome: poor maternal health outcomes (including hemorrhage, infections, hysterectomy, uterine rupture, and prolonged hospital stay)
cohort: The study included 354 women who delivered by cesarean section in public hospitals of Gamo, Gofa, and South Omo Zones in Southern Ethiopia between March 1 and April 30, 2022.
finding: The prevalence of poor maternal outcomes was 19.5%, with low hematocrit, referral from other institutions, presence of medical illness, delivery in primary hospitals, no ANC follow-up, and general anesthesia for surgery being independently associated factors.
mod_finding: Undergoing cesarean section under general anesthesia was independently associated with an increased odds of poor maternal health outcomes.
cross-section timing: Data were collected between March 1 and April 30, 2022, among women who delivered by cesarean section during that period.
